They then chain five angle facts: the co-interior angle with the 110° gives 70°, the reflex 240° converts to 120° by angles at a point, the 120° is split into 70° and 50°, the 50° transfers by alternate angles, and the 95° is split to leave 45°. The reflex angle and the need to split the angles at V and W are extra decisions beyond p73-q8 and p73-q9a, which chain simple additive alternate-angle steps. content.prompt: In each case, decide if AB is parallel to CD. Give a reason why or why not.

answer.short: Yes, $AB\parallel CD$: corresponding angles are equal.
answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ-118^\circ&=62^\circ\end{align*}$$
The corresponding angle at the lower intersection is also $62^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

answer.short: No. The co-interior angles sum to $179^\circ$ instead of $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The lower-right angle at the lower intersection is vertically opposite the upper-left angle, so that upper-left angle is $105^\circ$.
$$74^\circ+105^\circ=179^\circ$$
The co-interior angles do not sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB$ is not parallel to $CD$.

answer.short: Yes. $x=15$, the angle $7x=105^\circ$, and the co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}5x&=75\\x&=15\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}7x&=7\times15^\circ\\7x&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
$$75^\circ+105^\circ=180^\circ$$
The co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

content.prompt: In each case, decide if AB is parallel to CD. Give a reason why or why not.

answer.short: Yes, $AB\parallel CD$: alternate angles are equal.
answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ-109^\circ&=71^\circ\end{align*}$$
This is the lower-left angle at the upper intersection. The alternate angle at the lower intersection is also $71^\circ$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

answer.short: No. The co-interior angles sum to $178^\circ$ instead of $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The upper-left angle at the upper intersection is vertically opposite its lower-right angle, so that lower-right angle is $114^\circ$.
$$114^\circ+64^\circ=178^\circ$$
The co-interior angles do not sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB$ is not parallel to $CD$.

answer.short: No. $x=19$, the angle $5x=95^\circ$, and the co-interior angles sum to $171^\circ$ instead of $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}4x&=76\\x&=19\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}5x&=5\times19^\circ\\5x&=95^\circ\end{align*}$$
$$76^\circ+95^\circ=171^\circ$$
The co-interior angles do not sum to $180^\circ$, so $AB$ is not parallel to $CD$.

content.prompt: Find the value of $x$. Notice that $212^\circ$ and $28^\circ$ are overlapping.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$, so the angle between the upper arm and the right-hand arm is:
$$\begin{align*}360-212-28&=120.\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}x+120&=180\\x&=60.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=60^\circ$.

payloads.replacement: **Corresponding** angle pairs are in matching positions at the two intersections: on the same side of the transversal, and both above or both below their lines.
**Alternate** angle pairs have one angle at each intersection. They are inside the lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.

Decide whether these lines are parallel.

If corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal or co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, the lines are parallel. Otherwise they are not parallel.

answer.short:
Blanks in order: $72$; vertically; $108$; straight; $108$; $108$; vertically; opposite.

$a=72^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles). $b=c=108^\circ$ since each makes a straight angle with $72^\circ$; also $c=b$ (vertically opposite angles).
answer.worked:
$a=72^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

$b+72^\circ=180^\circ$ (straight angle).

$$\begin{align*}b&=180^\circ-72^\circ\\b&=108^\circ\end{align*}$$

$c+72^\circ=180^\circ$ (straight angle).

$$\begin{align*}c&=180^\circ-72^\circ\\c&=108^\circ\end{align*}$$

$c=b=108^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles), agreeing with the straight-angle calculation.

answer.short:
Blanks in order: $180$; $34$; $146$; vertically; straight; $34$; $34$; vertically; opposite.

$x=z=34^\circ$ since each makes a straight angle with $146^\circ$. $y=146^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles). Also $z=x$ (vertically opposite angles).

$x+146^\circ=180^\circ$ (straight angle).

$$\begin{align*}x&=180^\circ-146^\circ\\x&=34^\circ\end{align*}$$

$y=146^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

$z+146^\circ=180^\circ$ (straight angle).

$$\begin{align*}z&=180^\circ-146^\circ\\z&=34^\circ\end{align*}$$

$z=x=34^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles), agreeing with the straight-angle calculation.

content.prompt:
$OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$.
Work out the size of $\angle AOC$

answer.worked:
$OB$ bisects $\angle AOC$.
$$\begin{align*}5x+8&=7x-10\\18&=2x\\x&=9\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=(5\times9+8)^\circ\\\angle AOB&=53^\circ\\\angle BOC&=(7\times9-10)^\circ\\\angle BOC&=53^\circ\\\angle AOC&=53^\circ+53^\circ\\\angle AOC&=106^\circ\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: The student sets the two algebraic angle expressions equal using the bisector, solves a linear equation with x on both sides, then doubles to get the whole angle. This is the same demand as p71-q8.

content.prompt:
$OQ$ is the bisector of $\angle POR$.
Work out the size of $\angle POR$

answer.worked:
$OQ$ bisects $\angle POR$.
$$\begin{align*}3x+10&=6x-35\\45&=3x\\x&=15\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle POQ&=(3\times15+10)^\circ\\\angle POQ&=55^\circ\\\angle QOR&=(6\times15-35)^\circ\\\angle QOR&=55^\circ\\\angle POR&=55^\circ+55^\circ\\\angle POR&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Bisector gives 3x+10=6x-35. The student solves the linear equation, substitutes back and doubles to get the whole angle. This matches p71-q8 in steps and demand.
